layout: Upright handwritten sheet, 1678 by 2362 pixels. Author number 13 top centre, separate 28 lower left. Twenty-two principal baseline rows, including two numerical-evaluation rows, set display, generator lower definitions, and four relation rows; four additional insertion rows (top de{1,tau}, par rho, quatre, donc parenthesis); two number-only marginal rows. The word relations shares the height of the first relation row. Final generator proposal and relations cancelled by long diagonals. No genuine drawing or diagram apart from vertical equalities.

changes.evidence: The addition contains only de and the braced pair. Its d has a small loop and the e a short rightward exit; there is no u cup, no second relèvements, and no textual parenthesis. The curved stroke attaches the addition between relèvements and sont. The tau dot is treated separately below.
A dark isolated dot lies immediately above the tau crossbar. It is comparable in darkness and size to the dots over sigma elsewhere on the page, and is not a paper speck.
Root crop shows the subscript 1 directly followed by et, without a second punctuation mark. The comma after tau_0 is distinct.

changes.evidence: The tall descender of p, low compressed ar strokes, then rho's loop and descender are visible. The curved insertion stroke attaches this phrase after conjugués. There is no comma after rho; the comma is after the following tau-dot-sigma-infinity.

The initial relèvemen- is visible, though compressed. At the end, a tall t stroke is crossed by a dark terminal hook which can be a final s, as in the earlier relèvements, but the final ts cannot be separated with certainty. The plural is the leading reading, retained as doubtful rather than supplied from grammar.

The second word starts with a long looped f descending well below the baseline; low au, looped d, and terminal rait are visible, so faudrait rather than voudrais. The initial two-letter group has a broad upper stroke and crossed lower loop; Il is plausible but the distinction from Je is not secure from this single occurrence.

After the hyphen there is a shallow two-shouldered m with a separate horizontal bar above it. The lower stroke is not the straight lower shaft of an equality sign. This is an abbreviation, not the fully written word même.

After calligraphic E are two tall joined t strokes sharing a crossbar: tt, without letters ou. The next word has low en, an upright t, a separate i dot, and a low er exit: entier. There is no initial n or the repeated long sequence required for notamment.

The first line ends qu'on va: the small v and oval a are separately visible after qu'on. The next baseline begins relever, with initial r, tall looped l, and trailing r. The two words are not a single relève.

The word above the baseline has a q with a long descender, compact ua, tall t, and re exit. The insertion curve descends between les and générateurs. There is neither a g nor an abbreviation point after it.

The loop and descender suggest rho, but several short dark diagonal hatches obscure the upper part and any prime/dot. These local hatches are distinct from the long diagonal block cancellation. The underlying symbol is not resolved; a separate local deletion is recorded.

After the equality, rho has an open loop and long hooked descender. The following symbol retains the crossbar and curved lower stroke of tau despite the large diagonal strike crossing the block. I do not find a separate local cancellation of this tau beyond the block cancellation. Root retains the uncertainty about an additional local cancellation in place; the legible tau is first.

notes: The page continues an argument about lifts of involutions and fixed sets. It evaluates dotted sigma_1 and tau dotted sigma_1 at 2, identifies the fixed set with the unit circle minus 1, and states that this contains P and its conjugate and gives no new lifts beyond the one already obtained.

The author then asks for a presentation of the entire calligraphic E by generators and relations, starting from Gamma written as a form of S_3 times Z/2. The proposed generator list, parenthetical consequences for rho-prime, and relation system are cancelled and transcribed as cancelled work.
The struck involution relation uses 1,2,3 while the generator list uses 0,1,infinity. This mismatch prompted inspection; the ink still reads 1,2,3 and is not corrected.
The top added braced pair has dotted tau, unlike undotted tau in most formulas below. This local ink distinction is preserved; no cross-page convention was inferred.
After E the abbreviation is tt; after quand- it is barred m. Neither is expanded.
No external mathematical source, OCR, text recognition, or TeX compilation was used. These notes describe transcription and internal inspection, not an independent proof check.

The top number is 13 and the lower-left number is 28; both are retained, without inferring the origin of the secondary pagination. H’s editorial note already recognizes cancellation of the whole final proposal, so that fact alone is not counted as a substantive disagreement. Visual-reading events are preserved in the page report, not misclassified as mathematical CHECK_EVENTS.

adjudications.evidence: The raised de, braces, numeral 1 and dotted tau are visible, with the dot separate above the tau bar. The two readings differ only in TeX grouping braces.

Both short connectors have a low open e-like entry followed by the compressed n join. Their long exit strokes can resemble un at small scale; the cropped strokes remain consistent with en in both places. Tau subscripts 0, 1 and infinity are unchanged.

The three sigma letters carry distinct upper dots, and par rho sits above the baseline with an insertion leader. Subscripts 1, infinity and 0 and the enclosing punctuation match. Only macro grouping differs.

The first equality ends in an inline 1/2; the second is written on a separate lower line with a stacked 1 over 2. Dotted sigma, the argument 2 and both equality signs agree. Display wrappers and fraction braces account for the comparison difference.
The superscript has tau followed by a dotted sigma with subscript 1. The set braces, bar over the second z, equality to 1 and final set difference are visible. Only dot-command grouping differs.

The word relèvement is recoverable, but its far-right ending contains an extra crowded turn beyond the long join. The t and any following s cannot be cleanly separated. The singular-only second reading does not settle that cluster; the existing plural/singular doubt is retained.
A single wavy tilde is separate above sigma, with subscript 1 below-right. Tilde versus widetilde and grouping braces encode the same visible sign.
The separate dot above sigma, subscript 1, following tau and terminal point are clear. The only difference is dot-command grouping.

The initial capital has a long upper arm and a looped lower return; the following short curved stroke can be read as l, but its junction remains compatible with the earlier Je alternative. Il stays preferred, with the local ambiguity retained instead of resolved by the sentence.

After quand and its hyphen, the ink is a short m-shaped run with one separate horizontal bar above it. There is no written sequence of the additional letters in même. The literal barred-m shorthand is retained.

The short form has two tall t strokes joined near their feet; no oute sequence is written. In the following word, the tall t and dot over i are followed by a low ending that stops in an r-like down-hook; no additional final e is separable. Retain tt entier despite the grammatically expected feminine form.

The ornate S has an enclosing sweep and inner loop, with a distinct subscript 3; the script/fraktur distinction remains uncertain in this hand. The second reader confirms the preferred fraktur choice but does not remove the visual alphabet ambiguity. Gamma, product sign, Z/2 and comma agree.

The entire displayed group is crossed by broad diagonal cancellation strokes. The initial rho-shaped sign also has its own dense local crossing, beyond the global deletion; the prime/dot details remain obscured. The extra tau-like sign before the first lifted sigma is darkly overworked and remains a doubtful local deletion. Three lifted dotted sigmas, their subscripts and the vertical double-stroke identifications below are visible. Retain the finer cancellation distinctions and existing narrow doubts; the alternative underset constructions encode the same vertical layout.

The raised parenthesis is crossed along with the larger presentation. Its rho-prime powers 6, 3 and 2, the equalities, tau and final rho power -1 agree. The script reports only TeX grouping differences in the prime/exponent notation.

The whole four-line system remains crossed. The first-row indices read 1, 2 and 3; the second-row products use 0, 1 and infinity; the lower powers 6 and 3 are visible. At the overworked second-row right end, the final 2 is clear but crossing strokes prevent a secure recovery of the prior numeral or the dot/prime state. The second reading proposes a canceled -2 where the first proposed -1; neither hidden numeral can be certified. Retain the whole existing unsure expression and record this additional unresolved possibility, without silently fixing a revision sequence. Other differences are grouping and layout macros.
The light footer is 28, with a curved 2 and two-loop 8. Both readings agree on the digits; mspage is the established pagination macro, whereas the independent reader used a general margin wrapper.
